newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's parliament starts session on election.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's parliament starts session on election.

text.p: Serbia's parliament began an extraordinary session on Tuesday to consider a bill reinstating opposition victories in municipal elections last November.
Reporters were able to watch closed-circuit television showing 147 parliamentarians gather in the 250-seat assembly.

President Slobodan Milosevic's Socialists had annulled opposition victories in 14 towns and cities, including Belgrade, on grounds of "irregularities". The action prompted three months of protests and attracted strident international criticism.
A week ago Milosevic suddenly announced he was asking parliament to approve a bill recognising the opposition gains.
Opposition parties were quick to claim the climbdown as their triumph. State-run media emphasised the need to repair Serbia's ties with Western powers.
Milosevic's Socialists have 123 parliamentarians, but they have usually had their way with the support of ethnic minority representatives.

There were three proposals or draft laws on the agenda on Tuesday ahead of the crucial vote on the opposition's election wins and there was no way of knowing what time the issue would be brought to the vote.

The Radicals, a party of ulra-nationalists with 35 MPs, have submitted draft amendments challenging the bill, saying it allows the international community to use parliament to legalise decrees imposed from above.
